title: Derived lower shriek of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of
schemes. For a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{i}\bar X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$ of $f$
([sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]) the *derived lower shriek attached to $c$* is the
composite of derived functors

$$
Rf^c_!:=Rg_*\circ D(i_!)\colon D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}),
\qquad
R^+f^c_!:=R^+g_*\circ D^+(i_!)\colon D^+(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})\to D^+(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}),
$$

where $D(i_!)$, $D^+(i_!)$ apply the exact extension by zero of module objects
([sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]) levelwise ([sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]) and $Rg_*$, $R^+g_*$ are the derived
pushforwards of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. For $f$ admitting a
compactification, $Rf_!:=Rf^c_!$ and $R^+f_!:=R^+f^c_!$ for the chosen
compactification $c$ of $f$. The bounded below functors are the restrictions of the
unbounded ones: $R^+f^c_!$ agrees with $Rf^c_!$ on $D^+(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$.

This construction applies the derived-functor construction to the factors separately;
it does not define $Rf^c_!$ by deriving the underived composite
$f^c_!=g_*\circ i_!$. No assertion that these constructions differ for every
compactification is intended. For a module object $M$ placed in degree zero,
$H^0(Rf^c_!M)\cong g_*i_!M=f^c_!M$.

proof.text: For a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{i}\bar X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$, use the composites in [def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek-compactification] and [def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek-compactification-plus]. For a chosen compactification use [def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek-chosen] and the current [def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek-chosen-plus]. These give all four functors with exactly the stated source and target categories; in particular the last definition explicitly identifies $R^+f_!$ with $R^+g_*\circ D^+(i_!)$ for that chosen $c$.

Check the hypotheses for the general derived-functor comparison. For each $T=X,\bar X,Y$, the module objects of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] are sheaves of modules over the ring sheaf $\Lambda_T$. Indeed, by the sheafified tensor product in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], a sheaf action $\Lambda_T\otimes M\to M$ is exactly a compatible family of bilinear sectionwise actions; the two module axioms give the usual sectionwise module axioms, and the linear morphisms coincide. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] applies to the small pro-etale site (in a universe containing it), giving a Grothendieck abelian category. By [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] it has enough injectives, and the Right derived functors clause of the current [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] gives K-injective resolutions for each of these Grothendieck abelian categories. Use the localization universes fixed in that statement; no claim of a small derived category in the original object universe is needed. Finally the pushforward clause of the current [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], specialized to $g\colon\bar X\to Y$, defines $g_*=\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_g}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(g^{\Ab}_*)$ and explicitly states that this functor is additive and left exact. Its general commutative condensed coefficient ring and arbitrary scheme-morphism hypotheses are exactly those in force here. These are precisely the abelianness, injective-resolution and additivity hypotheses needed in the next step.

source.place: second factor: hypotheses of the general comparison made explicit

proof.text: By [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek], $i_!$ is exact and additive. In particular it preserves kernels, images and their quotients, so $H^n(i_!K)\cong i_!H^n(K)$; termwise application preserves quasi-isomorphisms and the condition of cohomology vanishing below a bound. With the localization and termwise $D(F)$ convention of the current [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], it therefore induces $D(i_!)$ directly and restricts to $D^+(i_!)$. Both $\iota_{\bar X}\circ D^+(i_!)$ and $D(i_!)\circ\iota_X$ are induced by the same termwise functor on complexes, giving their canonical natural isomorphism. The respective existence hypotheses in that statement's Exact functors clause are satisfied on the right-derived side by step 2; this argument does not invoke a left-derived functor or K-flat resolutions. Apply [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility] to $F=g_*$, with the abelian-category, universe, enough-injectives, K-injective-resolution and additivity hypotheses verified in step 2. Since [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] defines $R^+g_*$ and $Rg_*$ as these general derived functors of the module-object pushforward, this gives $\iota_Y\circ R^+g_*\cong Rg_*\circ\iota_{\bar X}$. This uses the comparison theorem's natural isomorphism, rather than just an objectwise agreement of resolutions.

Paste the natural isomorphisms of step 3: $\iota_Y\circ R^+g_*\circ D^+(i_!)\cong Rg_*\circ\iota_{\bar X}\circ D^+(i_!)\cong Rg_*\circ D(i_!)\circ\iota_X$. By [def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek-compactification] and [def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek-compactification-plus], the outside composites are $\iota_Y\circ R^+f^c_!$ and $Rf^c_!\circ\iota_X$. Substitute the chosen compactification, using [def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek-chosen] and the current [def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek-chosen-plus], to obtain $\iota_Y\circ R^+f_!\cong Rf_!\circ\iota_X$ as well.

source.place: chosen compactification specialization; previous proof final sentence gives the pasting

proof.text: For a module object $M$ in degree zero, exactness of $i_!$ in [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek] identifies $D(i_!)(M[0])$ with $(i_!M)[0]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] to $(i_!M)[0]$ with lower bound zero, obtaining a complex $I$ of injectives with $I^n=0$ for $n<0$ and $QI\cong(i_!M)[0]$; enough injectives was checked in step 2. Taking zeroth cohomology identifies $i_!M\cong\ker(I^0\to I^1)$, so composing this isomorphism with the kernel inclusion supplies the augmentation $i_!M\to I^0$. The vanishing of the other cohomology objects makes $0\to i_!M\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$ exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], this resolution also computes the unbounded derived pushforward in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Apply the left exactness in the current pushforward clause of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] to the augmented sequence at $I^0$. It gives $\ker(g_*I^0\to g_*I^1)\cong g_*i_!M$. There is no negative-degree term, so this kernel is $H^0(Rg_*i_!M)$. The composite definition [def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek-compactification] and the underived definition [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] now give $H^0(Rf^c_!M)\cong f^c_!M$. This degree-zero identity does not identify the two derived constructions.
